punchline: Peter Thiel's favorite interview question trips up most candidates, because their bold answers are things lots of people already believe.
thirty_sec: Peter Thiel asks every job candidate the same thing: what important truth do very few people agree with you on? The answers he hears most are that education is broken, that America is exceptional, or that there's no God. He calls them all bad, since plenty of people already agree or it's an old debate. A good answer sounds like: most people believe x, but the truth is the opposite. His own is that technology matters more than globalization.
